debate_title: AI governance frameworks for advanced AI systems

conflicts.point: Whether pre-market independent audits and safety gating effectively reduce systemic risks versus merely imposing harmful administrative delays.

positions.stance: Pre-market audits impose severe administrative delays that cost thousands of preventable deaths by slowing medical and technical innovation while offering negligible safety gains over decentralized open-source iteration.
Independent pre-market safety reviews are essential to prevent catastrophic system failures and unverified model deployments in high-stakes settings, similar to aviation and pharmaceutical standards.

conflicts.point: Whether existing tort law and discovery rules can adequately address algorithmic opacity without requiring invasive pre-market mandates.

positions.stance: Stretching product liability doctrines like Restatement Third of Torts Section 2(b) to cover withheld telemetry is legally untenable without specific statutory discovery rules for proprietary servers.
Withholding diagnostic telemetry from auditors constitutes an actionable design defect under existing product liability standards for complex opaque systems.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-market independent audits and safety gating effectively reduce systemic risks versus merely imposing harmful administrative delays.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist position prevails on empirical evidence because compute scaling trends offer verifiable capability benchmarks that are more easily tracked than subjective safety audits. Safety advocates rely on FDA analogies that do not cleanly map to software development cycles. Therefore, static pre-market gates risk lagging behind rapid technological changes.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical evidence demonstrating that pre-market audits successfully intercept catastrophic risks that escape post-market monitoring.

verdicts.conflict: Whether existing tort law and discovery rules can adequately address algorithmic opacity without requiring invasive pre-market mandates.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position prevails on implementation specificity because plaintiffs currently lack the pre-discovery access required to prove causation for black-box algorithmic systems under standard tort rules. Stretching product liability doctrines without statutory backing creates legal uncertainty. Thus, new legislation is necessary before courts can penalize withheld diagnostic telemetry.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Federal court rulings or new statutes establishing that withholding diagnostic telemetry constitutes a per se design defect under product liability law.
